items.title: Dow surges to record close as Big Tech pops; Trump calls off planned strikes against Iran
items.content: Dow Jones Industrial Average surged to a record close on Monday as major tech companies popped on first day of August trading, while oil prices declined after President Trump called off planned strikes against Iran.

items.title: Dow hits record high, jumping 693.38 points, buoyed by tech stocks and falling oil prices
items.content: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high on Monday, jumping 693.38 points, buoyed by rising tech stocks and falling oil prices.

items.title: Stocks rally near record as falling oil prices ease Wall Street's inflation worries
items.content: U.S. stocks rallied to the edge of their all-time high after easing oil prices helped calm Wall Street's worries that inflation could get even worse.

items.title: Dow soars over 700 points to end at record close as Big Tech surges, Mideast deal hopes grow
items.content: US stocks kicked off August on a strong note. Dow soared over 700 points to record close; S&P 500 near all-time high as Mideast deal hopes grew and oil retreated.

items.title: Trump says US 'locked and loaded' but agrees to hold off Iran strike; deal perimeter agreed
items.content: Trump said the US is 'locked and loaded and ready to go' against Iran, but agreed to requests by Iran and other Middle Eastern countries to hold off any attack as 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to'. Proposed agreement includes immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat; Israel joins the pause in strikes.

items.title: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis: tensions between Iran, US and Israel escalated from failed nuclear negotiations
items.content: Tensions between Iran, the United States and Israel escalated in the lead-up to 2026, stemming from failed nuclear negotiations in Geneva and a prior 12-day air conflict. Iran declared the Strait 'closed' from March 4, 2026, attacking ships attempting to transit.

items.title: China stocks slide as global AI selloff hits chipmakers; Alibaba rallies on new AI model
items.content: Chinese equities declined on Monday as a global selloff in AI-linked stocks weighed on semiconductor shares, while Hong Kong's technology sector outperformed, led by Alibaba after it released its latest AI model.

items.title: China stocks slide as AI selloff hammers chip supply chain; Alibaba jumps
items.content: China stocks fell on Monday as a global rout in AI-related shares dragged down semiconductor stocks, while Hong Kong's internet platforms bucked the trend, led by a jump in Alibaba after it released its latest AI model.

items.title: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy
items.content: AI-linked shares, particularly chipmakers, dropped around the world. China reported developing its own deep-ultraviolet lithography tools, challenging ASML's monopoly in the chip supply chain. South Korea's Kospi fell 11.5% on Tuesday and a further 6% on Wednesday, dragged down by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics.

items.title: US500 index at 7,524 points on August 2, +0.46% from previous session
items.content: The main US stock market index (US500) rose to 7,524 points on August 2, 2026, gaining 0.46%. Over the past month the index has declined 0.18%, though it remains 18.87% higher than a year ago.

items.title: This week in markets: SpaceX's first earnings report; chip and memory giants; jobs report
items.content: SpaceX to post Q2 2026 results and host webcast on August 4, 2026 (its first earnings report). Week also features earnings from chip and memory giants and the US jobs report.

items.title: June 2026 PCE inflation falls 0.1% m/m, consumer spending up 0.3%
items.content: US PCE price index decreased 0.1% month-over-month in June 2026, as expected, after a 0.5% rise in May. Goods prices fell 0.6% (most since Nov 2023); services inflation slowed to 0.1% from 0.5%. Annual PCE eased to 3.70% from 4.10% in May.

items.title: Chinese chip maker CXMT shares surge 466% on debut, biggest IPO since 2010, raising $8.6B
items.content: CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies) raised at least $8.6 billion, priced at 8.66 yuan per share, listing on Shanghai's STAR market. Shares surged 466% on first day of trading as the AI boom continues.

items.title: Earnings calendar for week Aug 3-7: SpaceX, Caterpillar, chip and memory giants
items.content: Wall Street calls for Caterpillar Q2 EPS of $6.20 (+31.4% YoY) on revenue of $19.2B (+15.7% YoY). Busiest days: 494 earnings on Wed Aug 5, 577 on Thu Aug 6 per Yahoo Finance calendar.
